reason: E2 shows that AlMo0.5NbTa0.5TiZr forms a bcc matrix and Al-Zr-rich intermetallics at high temperature, but it does not demonstrate coherent nanoscale precipitates, their coarsening resistance, or their role as irradiation defect sinks. E1 discusses enhanced radiation tolerance via compositional complexity in Ni-based equiatomic alloys, not in refractory HEAs or via precipitates. The key premises about precipitate-mediated strengthening and irradiation resistance in this specific alloy are unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: AlMo0.5NbTa0.5TiZr can form a B2+bcc matrix with nanoscale precipitates upon aging
Nanoscale precipitates in this alloy can be coherent and resist coarsening up to ~900 °C
Nanoscale precipitates act as effective defect sinks to enhance irradiation tolerance
A short high-temperature anneal (~1150 °C, 1–2 h) can optimize precipitate dispersion without over-aging
Compositional complexity in HEAs promotes defect recombination and radiation tolerance
